correctness.rationale: The Skellam PMF, special zero-mass factor, Bessel Turán positivity, ratio decomposition, and hyperbolic factor were reconstructed. The positive Bessel series yields R_k(z)>=(k+1)^2/(k(k+1)+ab), and hyperbolic sine yields Q_k-1<1/k^2 for k>=2. Their exact comparison gives strict LC when ab<=1. For fixed index the Bessel integral concentration yields R_k->1, while Q_k>1 at nonzero fixed imbalance, establishing all arbitrarily long finite violating runs; an explicit polynomial lower bound against exponential decay proves eventual strict LC. The exact rational-tail checker passed at rates 3,12, and no finite test is treated as proof of universal quantifiers. The classical Bessel Turán integral formula is independently justified by Neumann’s product identity.

originality.rationale: Targeted mathematical-record and published-source searches, combined with comparison against recoverable prior claims, found no covering result. The mathematical claim concerns the curvature of the sign-forgotten absolute difference of unequal Poisson counts, not signed differences, order statistics, Skellam process transforms, or Bessel Turán positivity alone. Signed Bessel log-concavity supplies one input but does not dominate the positive hyperbolic-cosine folding factor. A 2022 Skellam review and a 2020 primary Skellam-process article were inspected for the same object. No matching classification or arbitrary-run curvature result was found; an equivalent older treatment remains possible.

The full text of older Skellam approximation literature and the foundational Bessel survey was not compared exhaustively; no independent priority confirmation has occurred.

value.rationale: Taking the absolute magnitude of count differences deliberately discards sign information. The theorem determines a nontrivial universal protected region in two-rate intensity space and, in a single natural family, proves arbitrary-duration failure and eventual recovery of adjacent-mass log-concavity. This structural contrast matters when using log-concave count models or shape-constrained methods for unsigned comparative count data. The exact counterexample and analytic interval mechanism are not merely numerical or cosmetic modifications of signed Skellam log-concavity. No global sharp cutoff beyond the stated sufficient region is claimed. The high-intensity violations can lie in low-probability regions, so the result is valued as a structural boundary rather than a general central-mass effect.
